extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
extraction.description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and Project Gutenberg text data. It consists of 8 languages (English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Polish) totaling around 50.5K hours of speech, along with Language Models and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audiobooks were downloaded from LibriVox using data preparation tools from the Libri-Light library. Corresponding text sources for the audiobooks were downloaded using automated parsers for popular domains (such as gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org) or retrieved via manual approaches, text extraction from PDF/EPUB via pdftotext, and manual online searches for alternate sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Audiobooks with corrupted metadata (missing title or information about speakers and authors) were removed. Audiobooks with multiple speakers ('Dramatic Reading') were removed. Candidate transcripts were discarded if the WER between the candidate transcript and pseudo label exceeded 40%.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audiobooks from LibriVox and text sources from Project Gutenberg, Archive.org, CCEL, HathiTrust, Spiegel.de, Zeno.org, and other online domains.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: To address numbers in audiobook texts, matched text from books was aligned with pseudo labels, and numbers in the text were replaced with the corresponding aligned spoken words from the pseudo labels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz and segmented into 10–20 second chunks based on silence intervals detected using acoustic models in wav2letter@anywhere. Pseudo labels were generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram LM. Source text was split into overlapping documents (1250 words, stride 1000) and aligned to pseudo labels via TF-IDF bigram similarity and Smith-Waterman alignment. Heuristics were applied to replace rare word forms, hyphens, and apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization was performed using NFKC normalization, removing unwanted characters (punctuations, subscripts/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), stripping end-of-line hyphens to join split words, and filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges defined by each language's orthography.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts for training data were automatically retrieved from source book texts by matching acoustic model pseudo labels via Smith-Waterman alignment. For the development and test sets, human transcribers conducted verification by listening to audio while reviewing transcripts and correcting clear and obvious errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Table 3 evaluates the word error rate (WER) between generated transcripts and human rated transcripts across languages on dev and test sets (ranging from 1.93% on Spanish dev to 12.64% on Portuguese dev). Transcribers were instructed to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid adding bias.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: wav2letter@anywhere, Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolution models with ASG/CTC loss, 4-gram Language Models, KenLM toolkit, pdftotext, SVM gender classifier
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (predicted using an SVM classifier trained on acoustic features), voice audio recordings
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to promote open research in large-scale multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) research by providing open-license multilingual resources.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LibriVox audio data is heavily dominated by English. In development and test sets, speakers are balanced in gender and duration. Potential human annotation bias was mitigated by instructing verifiers to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Number replacement heuristic relying on pseudo labels may not always yield correct transcriptions; high out-of-vocabulary rate (13.39%) in Polish language model; availability and text quality vary widely across non-English languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems; multilingual ASR; limited-supervision/low-resource speech recognition benchmarking; Text-To-Speech (TTS) research; Language Modeling
